scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9012: Hi IT!! Everything to do with the partner network is
like WADING THROUGH TREACLE today -- from my machine pc1 (195.11.14.2) their
system (200.1.1.2) takes FOREVER to respond. The line between us and the
partner is obviously COMPLETELY CONGESTED -- everything squeezes through that
one link and it is jammed solid!! Please unclog the partner line (or get a
WIDER one) and speed my connection back up!!! I can't submit anything like
this!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — extreme slowness reaching the partner network
(200.1.1.2/pc2) from pc1 (195.11.14.2) — is not corroborated by any
measurable network fault. A full end-to-end inspection of every component
in the path shows a completely healthy network.

Reachability: ICMP ping from pc1 to pc2 across both routers returns ~1 ms
RTT with zero packet loss over 10 consecutive probes. TCP throughput via
iperf3 achieves 148 Mbit/s with only 23 TCP retransmits in five seconds,
which is normal behaviour for a single flow over a shared virtual
environment.

Data plane: All four interfaces (router1:eth0/eth1 and router2:eth0/eth1)
carry the default Linux fq_codel qdisc with no rate cap, no netem delay
emulation, no HTB/tbf shaping, and zero dropped or queued packets.
router1:eth0 — the inter-router "partner link" specifically named in the
ticket — is a 10 Gbps full-duplex virtual link with no congestion
whatsoever.

Control plane: BGP sessions between AS 1 (router1) and AS 2 (router2) are
fully established. router1 correctly learns 200.1.1.0/24 via BGP, and
router2 correctly learns 195.11.14.0/24 via BGP. Both routes are installed
in the FIB. System resources on both routers are idle (100% CPU idle, 3%
disk used).

Root cause: There is no network fault. The partner link is not congested and
no misconfiguration exists on any device.

Corrective action: No network change is required. The helpdesk ticket should
be closed as a false report. The user's perceived slowness should be
investigated at the application or endpoint layer (e.g., server-side
processing time, client-side DNS resolution, browser caching) rather than
the network.
